standing: Education Act Cap. 41 gives the vernacular no standing and no language-promotion clause
Its only three uses of language are offences of abusive language to teachers and officers
PEER's language section records only conversational Spanish in primary, a foreign language
mediumOfInstruction: Education Act Cap. 41 has no medium-of-instruction clause; curriculum is left to regulations
Its three uses of language are all offence provisions about abusive language to staff
PEER names no language of instruction; its only entry is primary conversational Spanish
taughtAsSubject: Education Act Cap. 41 names no language as a subject; subjects are left to regulations
The Act's three uses of language are offence provisions, not curriculum
PEER records only a conversational Spanish programme in primary schools, since 1997

sources.label: Barbados, Education Act, Cap. 41 (L.R.O. 2002 consolidation) — long title, the Minister's regulation-making power over the curriculum of study, and ss. 62 and the search provisions, the Act's only three uses of the word language

taughtAsSubject: Education Act Cap. 86 names no language as a school subject at any level
It leaves core and foundation subjects to a national curriculum the Minister must establish
Its only language clause is goal (g), on the history, language and culture of Grenadians

standing: The Education Act 2006 gives no language a standing of its own
It names language only at goal (g), on understanding Vincentian history and culture
PEER cites the EFA 2015 review: no distinct ethnic minorities despite a heterogeneous population
